spans.s:
Tuṣa, in the Atharvaveda and later, regularly denotes the ‘husk’ of grain, often used for a fire.
Foot notes ix. 6, 16; xi. 1, 12, 29; 3, 5; xii. 3, 19.
taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 6, 5, 5; aitareya brāhmaṇa, ii. 7, 9, etc.
tuṣa-pakva, taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 2, 4, 2; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 2, 4; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, vii. 2, 1, 7.

Tūṣa is found in the later Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas denoting the ‘fringe’ or ‘trimming’ of a garment.
Foot notes taittirīya Saṃhitā, i. 8, 1, 1; ii. 4, 9, 1; vi. 1, 1, 3; kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xxiii. 1; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 6, 1, 8; pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, xvii. 1, etc.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 262.
